found_by: reports/c46_trick_attacker_item_gap.json, as the reason a confirmed engine fix cleared zero rows
the_defect: evaluate_boundary_strict reports an engine-side itemleftovers component that the engine's instruction stream does not contain. Demonstrated in a single process on s18100475/78: generate_instructions returns [Switch SideTwo, SetLastUsedMove x2, Heal SideTwo 14, Damage SideOne 80, ChangeSideCondition SideOne ToxicCount] with the engine's p1 going 85 -> 5, exactly matching the observed 5 -- while the differential on the same row and the same states reports p1 attributed components differ: observed_only=[] engine_only=[('itemleftovers', 16)].
why_it_matters: The component decomposition is what the whole certification residue is measured in. A phantom component means some unattributed rows describe a disagreement that does not exist in the engine, and no engine fix can ever clear them.
scope_not_yet_known: 9 rows are confirmed to carry it. Whether it reaches further into the 485 is unmeasured and must not be assumed.
next: trace how the differential derives itemleftovers -- from the instruction stream, from an HP-delta heuristic, or from maxhp/16 inference -- and on which state it evaluates it.
why: There is no phantom component. The differential calls pokezero_search.branch_events, a separate native build that was stale; it was reporting the OLD engine's Leftovers tick accurately. Rebuilding both consumers cleared 8 of the 9 rows. See reports/c46_trick_attacker_item_gap.json.
